title: Arrays in C#
intro: Catch up on the key A Level ideas. Complete four retrieval questions, work through the examples, then practise and explain your reasoning.

questions.prompt: For a 3 × 3 array called board, what do GetLength(0) and GetLength(1) return?
options: 2 and 3.
3 and 3.
4 and 3.
questions.feedback: Model answer: 3 and 3. Explanation: Dimension 0 is rows; dimension 1 is columns.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between a function and a procedure?
questions.answer: A function returns a value; a procedure does not.
options: A function returns a value; a procedure does not.
A function returns a value; a procedure does always.
There is not enough information to determine the result.
questions.feedback: Model answer: A function returns a value; a procedure does not.

questions.prompt: Why must every value in a C# string[,] array be stored as a string?
questions.answer: An array has one declared element type, so every element must be compatible with that type.
options: There is not enough information to determine the result.
An array has one declared element type, so every element must be compatible with that type.
An array has one declared element type, so every element need not be compatible with that type.
questions.feedback: Model answer: An array has one declared element type, so every element must be compatible with that type.

blocks.title: Key vocabulary
items: Array — A fixed collection of elements accessed using indexes.
Element — One stored value inside an array.
Index — The position number used to access an array element.
Dimension — One direction or level used to locate an element.
[] — C# syntax for an array with one dimension.
[,] — C# syntax for an array with two dimensions.

blocks.title: 1D · one index
blocks.text: Indexes start at 0, so students[2] is Charlie.

blocks.title: 2D · row and column
blocks.text: [0,0] means row 0, column 0. It outputs Amelia.

blocks.title: GetLength() names the dimension
blocks.text: For the array above, the answers are 3 and 2.

blocks.title: 3D · layer, row, column
blocks.text: Read the indexes as layer → row → column. A 3D array is easiest to visualise as several 2D tables stacked together.

blocks.title: Worked example · Build studentResults
blocks.text: Store each student's name and score in a 2D array, then display every row. Amelia 72 Ben 65 Charlie 81
